claims.text: The studied alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Overall tribo-corrosion degradation is governed by competition between passive-film removal during sliding and repassivation kinetics.
Sliding wear mechanically removes the protective passive oxide film.
When mechanical film removal outpaces repassivation, localized corrosion accelerates.
The native passive film on equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is Cr/Al-rich.
The native alloy surface is passivated by a naturally formed thin oxide film.
Actively sliding regions will be compared with static immersion-only regions under the same environment.
Testing will be conducted in 3.5 wt% NaCl at controlled load and sliding speed.
Passive-film formation, abrasion, and repair mediate coupling between mechanical wear and electrochemical corrosion.
Continuous abrasion of the passive film occurs during tribological wear.
Film removal faster than film reformation creates local galvanic conditions.
The proposed local galvanic conditions greatly accelerate corrosion.
Sufficiently rapid repassivation can maintain surface protection despite intermittent film removal.
Sliding regions in which oxide removal exceeds repassivation will have greater total degradation than static immersed regions.
The greater total degradation in sliding regions will include increased wear loss and localized corrosion.
The prediction applies when mechanical abrasion dominates film removal and passive-film reformation is rate-limited.
The prediction may fail or be masked if external stimuli induce unusually rapid repassivation.
Temperature or pH changes may mask the prediction by significantly altering corrosion kinetics.
Oxide thickness recovery during non-worn intervals can be used to measure repassivation rate.

The mechanism would be falsified if substantial mechanical disruption produced no change in film dynamics or no significant difference in corrosion current and total degradation between worn and static regions.

contradictions.description: The alloy is specified as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and therefore contains no stated Al, yet its passive film is repeatedly described as Al-rich. No Al source, alloy modification, coating, or contamination pathway is provided.
